record.paper_title: Semigroups of rational functions: some problems and conjectures
record.original_question: Let P be a non-special rational function of degree at least two, and let E(P) be the semigroup consisting of rational functions Q of degree at least two that share the measure of maximal entropy μ_P with P, together with the μ_P-invariant Möbius transformations. Is it true that there exist finitely many rational functions X_1, …, X_r such that X belongs to E(P) if and only if X = X_j∘P^{∘k} for some j with 1 ≤ j ≤ r and some k ≥ 0?

evidence.quote: For a rational function P of degree at least two, we denote by μ_P the measure of maximal entropy for P, and by E(P) the set of rational functions Q of degree at least two such that μ_Q = μ_P, completed by μ_P-invariant Möbius transformations. The set E(P) is a semigroup.

Conjecture 3.5. Let P be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Then there exist finitely many rational functions X1, X2, . . . , Xr such that X belongs to E(P) if and only if X = Xj ∘ P^{∘k} for some j, 1 ≤ j ≤ r, and k ≥ 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\hat{\mathbb{C}}$ denote the Riemann sphere. For a rational function $P:\hat{\mathbb{C}}\to\hat{\mathbb{C}}$ of degree at least two, let $\mu_P$ denote its (unique) measure of maximal entropy. Recall that $P$ is called special if either $P$ is conjugate, via a Möbius transformation, to $z^{\pm n}$ or to a Chebyshev polynomial $\pm T_n$, or $P$ is a Lattès map (induced by an endomorphism of an elliptic curve).

Define
$$E(P) \;=\; \{Q : Q \text{ is a rational function of degree } \geq 2 \text{ with } \mu_Q = \mu_P\} \;\cup\; \{M \in \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C}) : M_*\mu_P = \mu_P\}.$$
It is known that $E(P)$ is a semigroup under composition.

Let $P^{\circ k}$ denote the $k$-th iterate of $P$ (with $P^{\circ 0} = \mathrm{id}$).

Question. Let $P$ be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Do there exist finitely many rational functions $X_1, X_2, \dots, X_r$ such that an element $X$ belongs to $E(P)$ if and only if
$$X = X_j \circ P^{\circ k}$$
for some $j \in \{1,\dots,r\}$ and some integer $k \geq 0$?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears in Pakovich's list of problems/conjectures on semigroups of rational functions. Subsequent work (e.g., Pakovich's "On amenable semigroups of rational functions") establishes related structural results (such as every subsemigroup of $E(P)$ being "power twisted" when $P$ is non-special) and confirms the conjecture in the polynomial case, but no source found resolves the full conjecture for arbitrary non-special rational $P$. The status appears to be open in the general rational case.

status_evidence.title: On amenable semigroups of rational functions
status_evidence.snippet: Every subsemigroup of the semigroup E(P), where P is a non-special rational function of degree at least two, is power twisted. Theorem 1.2 confirms in the polynomial case the conjecture proposed in [7].
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture has been confirmed in the polynomial case, but the rational case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Fedor Pakovich — publications
status_evidence.snippet: List of publications on semigroups of rational functions and their measure of maximal entropy.
status_evidence.claim: No paper resolving the full conjecture for arbitrary non-special rational P is listed.
